items.reason: runtimeutil.Budget.RecordUsage now charges provider-reported codex_rollout_budget_units directly (finite, non-negative or fatal error), falling back to weighted token accounting; mirrors Rust 8b8fa7276f (#36715).
Standard MCP catalog limit raised 1024->2048 and host-owned codex_apps (CodexAppsServerConfig) uses 8192 via per-server CatalogItemLimit; mirrors Rust e4e040881a (#36772).

Go exposes /fast only when fast_mode is enabled and the current model catalog contains a tier named fast. It toggles using that tier's actual ID versus default, persists the config alias fast, propagates the effective ID to local and remote turns, and reports persistence success/failure like Rust. Canonical /btw, /multi-agents, and /quit popup entries remain separate from aliases.

Rust /clear dispatches ClearUi, which starts a fresh session while keeping the previous rollout resumable. Go TUI and interactive command paths now reset thread identity, transcript, and idle status instead of only clearing visible messages.

Runtime-backed slash commands now execute real actions: /app launches the Codex Desktop thread deep link, /rollout reads the active thread rollout path, /sandbox-add-read-dir validates and adds a readable root, /import invokes external-agent detect/import RPCs, and /memories opens a dedicated settings modal with persisted memory edits.

Go validates and emits ordered initialItems notifications, stores codexResponseHandoffMode, and routes streamed assistant output from appserver turns into bounded realtime handoff_append itemAdded notifications. Commentary/final channels, final-message prefix, UTF-8-safe head/tail truncation, and client-managed/codexResponsesAsItems skips are covered.

Go rollout loading and doctor inventory now accept .jsonl.zst, map compressed siblings to canonical .jsonl state-DB keys, prefer plain rollouts, and report corrupt compressed files without false stale rows.
Go emits completion items directly from the active AgentLoopResult, which provides the same externally observable active-turn filtering without Rust's app-server notification backfill stage.

Go prepares model metadata and permission requirements locally before TUI startup, so the Rust parallel remote requests have no Go-side latency or scheduling counterpart; startup behavior is already equivalent.

Go detects external project Markdown memory, verifies SHA-256 content, imports under extension-scoped resources with scope.json and source/project/cwd/hash metadata, rejects path/hash failures, and removes resources for disappeared projects without inventing rollout provenance.
The Rust change removes an internal crate only; Go's realtime wire behavior remains covered and unchanged.

Linux Landlock/bwrap is verified on a native Kali runner. Native Windows platform and production ConPTY gates pass. Forty-seven relevant packages compile for Darwin/arm64, and Darwin network/sandbox vet plus actionlint pass. The macOS workflow now directly tests Keychain roots, a Unix-socket HTTP round trip, native seatbelt enforcement, and desktop/platform behavior; a native macOS workflow artifact is still required.

The opt-in Windows cancellation diagnostic still fails on Rust bbbf396839: Rust leaves the PowerShell descendant alive and the resumed turn aborts, while Go terminates the tree and resumes safely. Closing this requires an upstream Rust fix; Go must not regress process-tree safety to imitate the defect.

All 82 Rust commits from fa1d4c40d0 through 25eecb071e were classified. Applicable protocol, MCP, executor sandbox, tool registry, remote compaction, telemetry, TUI width, OAuth redirect, serialization, fork boundary, and lifecycle changes are implemented with focused and race coverage; Rust-only dependency, release, allocation, and source-layout changes are explicitly classified.
